section_summary: This section documents Allied occupation policy and Japanese domestic developments concerning public service labor rights, economic deconcentration, and post-surrender legal reforms between November 1948 and July 1949. It includes British and Japanese union objections to strike prohibitions under the National Public Service Law, State Department inquiries into Deconcentration Review Board standards and proposed antitrust revisions, and official despatches transmitting Diet amendments. The section concludes with an extensive alphabetical reference index prepared by GHQ SCAP's Legal Section cataloguing Japanese statutes enacted from 1946 through 1948.

subfiles.about: Relays British diplomatic representations and a Far Eastern Commission statement concerning strike prohibitions and independent arbitration under the proposed National Public Service Law revision.
subfiles.summary: Transmits British objections to an absolute strike ban in permanent Japanese civil service legislation, emphasizing the need for independent arbitration machinery.
subfiles.title: Department of State Outgoing Telegram to USPOLAD Tokyo Concerning British Views on National Public Service Legislation
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits a petition from the Kyoto University Workers' Union protesting the Japanese Government's use of MacArthur's letter to oppress public service labor unions.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits a petition from the Kyoto University Workers' Union alleging that the Japanese Government is using General MacArthur's letter to suppress union rights and demanding livelihood guarantees before revising the National Public Service Law.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 750: Union Petition Concerning Revision of National Public Service Law

subfiles.about: Transmits and explains Diet amendments extending Holding Company Liquidation Commission authority and transferring Zaibatsu Family Control review powers directly to the Prime Minister.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits translations of amendments to the Elimination of Excessive Concentrations of Economic Power Law and the Law for Termination of Zaibatsu Family Control. The deconcentration amendment extends the authority of the Holding Company Liquidation Commission until June 30, 1949 before transferring administration to the Fair Trade Commission. The Zaibatsu amendment abolishes the Appointees Examination and Reexamination Committees, transferring their review functions directly to the Prime Minister.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 755: Amendment of Deconcentration Law and Law for Termination of Zaibatsu Family Control

subfiles.about: Requests clarification of the Deconcentration Review Board's terms of reference and background information on its rulings to answer anticipated Far Eastern Commission and business inquiries.
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Requests essential background on Deconcentration Review Board rulings and terms of reference to prepare for Far Eastern Commission discussions and resolve American business uncertainties.
subfiles.title: Letter from Charles E. Saltzman to William H. Draper, Jr. Requesting Information on Deconcentration Review Board
subfiles.to: William H. Draper, Jr., Under Secretary of the Army

subfiles.about: Contains an earlier draft of the letter requesting DRB information, together with an enclosed draft cable to General MacArthur requesting DRB opinions and dissolution plans.
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Draft letter to Under Secretary Draper enclosing a proposed telegram asking General MacArthur to furnish DRB opinions and dissolution plans to Washington.
subfiles.title: Draft Letter from Charles E. Saltzman to William H. Draper, Jr. with Enclosed Draft Telegram to General MacArthur
subfiles.to: William H. Draper, Jr., Under Secretary of the Army

subfiles.about: Duplicate carbon copy of Assistant Secretary Saltzman's December 3, 1948 letter requesting DRB terms of reference and case rulings, bound with page two preceding page one.
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Duplicate carbon copy of Saltzman's letter requesting information on the Deconcentration Review Board's terms of reference and case rulings.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Copy of Letter from Charles E. Saltzman to William H. Draper, Jr.
subfiles.to: William H. Draper, Jr., Under Secretary of the Army

subfiles.about: Records the transfer of an Army Department letter dated January 17, 1949 from file number 894.50/1-1749 to 894.044/1-1749.
subfiles.from: Department of State Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: Transfer sheet recording transfer of an Army Department letter from file 894.50/1-1749 to 894.044/1-1749.
subfiles.title: Department of State Form DS-202 Transfer Sheet

subfiles.about: Expresses grave concern over proposed amendments to the Japanese Antitrust Law relaxing restrictions on intercorporate stockholdings, financial company holdings, interlocking directorates, and debentures.
subfiles.from: Roger C. Dixon, International Resources Division
subfiles.summary: Warns that proposed Diet amendments based on the Hutchinson report would weaken Japanese Antitrust Law prohibitions on stockholding and interlocking directorates, risking a revival of Zaibatsu-style business combinations.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Roger C. Dixon to Paul H. Nitze Concerning Pending Amendments of the Japanese Antitrust Law
subfiles.to: Paul H. Nitze, Deputy to the Assistant Secretary of State for Economic Affairs

subfiles.about: Transmits an extensive alphabetical index compiled by GHQ SCAP's Legal Section listing Japanese laws enacted in 1946, 1947, and 1948 with Official Gazette citations and amendment histories.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch transmitting five copies of an alphabetical index prepared by Jeanne D. Connors of GHQ SCAP Legal Section covering all Japanese laws enacted in 1946, 1947, and 1948. The index lists statutes with their law numbers, Official Gazette publication dates, and subsequent amendment histories across broad legal categories. A prefatory guide explains the indexing system and categorization rules used to facilitate referencing English translations of Diet legislation.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 469: Index to Japanese Laws, with Enclosed Alphabetical Index to 1946, 1947, and 1948 Laws
